data.one_liner: On-device face liveness detection, anti-spoofing, and Face ID for Flutter apps.
data.what_it_does: Provides real-time face liveness detection and anti-spoofing challenges like blinks, head turns, and smiles. Features persistent on-device Face ID embeddings using Google ML Kit, TensorFlow Lite, and optional YOLOv8 or SCRFD detectors.
use_when: You need secure, on-device user verification and KYC compliance via face recognition.
You want to prevent replay attacks and screen spoofs without routing biometric video to a server.
You need passive or active facial authentication flows with persistent local Face ID matching.
avoid_when: Your application targets environments below Android API 26 or iOS 13.
You require server-side cloud biometric storage rather than secure local device storage.
strengths: Runs entirely on-device with zero server calls for core liveness and replay checks.
Multi-signal replay attack detection and 9-signal anti-spoof engine.
Supports both active challenge gestures and passive zero-action Face ID sessions.
weaknesses: Requires platform permission setup and specific minimum OS and SDK versions.
Large binary or model dependencies (such as TFLite models) downloaded at runtime.
data.setup_notes: Requires setting camera permissions in AndroidManifest.xml and Info.plist, configuring minSdk 26 for Android, and potentially setting up dependency overrides for tflite_flutter.
data.minimal_example:
FlutterFaceLiveness(
  actions: [
    LivenessAction.blink,
    LivenessAction.turnLeft,
  ],
  config: LivenessConfig(
    randomizeActions: true,
    enableAntiSpoof: true,
  ),
  onSuccess: (result) => print('Success: ${result.sessionId}'),
  onFailed: (reason) => print('Failed: $reason'),
)
